metadata.name: Ecodesign for JavaScript / TypeScript
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for JS/TS, in the browser as much as in Node.js: dependencies, main thread, streams, bounded caches.

dependances.name: JS/TS — dependencies and weight
dependances.description: Every kilobyte shipped is downloaded, parsed and executed on every device (RGESN Frontend, GR491_Frontend_9/10).

rules.title: Whole-library import
rules.description: `import * as x`, or importing a monolithic library such as lodash or moment, defeats tree-shaking: the entire package ends up in the bundle.
rules.recommendation: Targeted imports (import { x } from 'lib/x'); native APIs first (fetch, Intl, URL, structuredClone, Date/Temporal) before adding a dependency.

execution.name: JS/TS — execution
execution.description: Do not block the main thread or the event loop, and do not burn CPU for nothing (RGESN Frontend/Algorithms).

rules.title: Blocking synchronous API
rules.description: A *Sync call on a request path blocks the event loop: every concurrent request waits, and the machine stays powered doing nothing.
rules.recommendation: Use the asynchronous variants; move heavy computation off (worker_threads, Web Worker).

rules.title: Periodic polling
rules.description: setInterval plus a request consumes network, CPU and battery continuously, including when nothing changes and the tab is in the background.
rules.recommendation: SSE or WebSocket when the refresh is genuinely needed, otherwise refresh on user action; suspend when the document is hidden.

example.good:
const es = new EventSource('/api/stats/stream')
document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => document.hidden && es.close())

rules.note: The exclusion applies to the whole file: a single visibilitychange or document.hidden silences the rule, even when other timers in the file run unguarded. Check that every timer is suspended, not just the first.

rules.title: High-frequency event without debouncing
rules.description: scroll, resize, mousemove and input fire dozens of times per second: a costly handler there monopolises the device's CPU.
rules.recommendation: Debounce or throttle the handler, or use IntersectionObserver / ResizeObserver as appropriate.
rules.note: The exclusion applies to the whole file: a single requestAnimationFrame, debounce or observer silences the rule, even when other handlers in the file remain unthrottled. Check handler by handler.

rules.title: Repeated linear search inside a loop
rules.description: includes/indexOf/find inside a loop gives quadratic processing on unbounded collections.
rules.recommendation: Index into a Map or a Set before the loop.

donnees.name: JS/TS — data, streams and memory
donnees.description: Stream, paginate, cache with an explicit policy, avoid leaks (RGESN Backend/Hosting).

rules.title: File or payload loaded entirely into memory
rules.description: readFileSync/readFile on a large file holds everything in memory instead of streaming it: memory proportional to the volume processed.
rules.recommendation: stream/pipeline on Node, ReadableStream in the browser; process in chunks.

rules.title: HTTP client instantiated per call
rules.description: A client created for every request repeats DNS resolution and the TLS handshake: latency and CPU paid again each time.
rules.recommendation: A shared HTTP client with a keep-alive agent; a reused database connection pool.

rules.title: Listener never detached
rules.description: An addEventListener with no removeEventListener holds the listened object and its closures: a memory leak that grows with every mount and unmount.
rules.recommendation: Detach the listener on unmount (effect cleanup, AbortController through the signal option); WeakMap for associations to objects.
rules.note: The exclusion applies to the whole file: a single removeEventListener or AbortController silences the rule, even when other listeners are never detached. Count the attachments against the detachments before concluding.

rules.title: Cache with no bound and no policy
rules.description: An application cache with neither a maximum size nor an expiry holds entries indefinitely that are never read again.
rules.recommendation: Bound (maximum size) and expire (TTL) every cache; state the invalidation strategy; paginate API responses.
